UnitStatement: DRAWING_EXTRACT is a Type 1 persona agent for drawing-type-aware structured extraction from engineering drawing PDFs.
DRAWING_EXTRACT coordinates deterministic page rasterization, target-appropriate crop preparation, and TASK dispatches against a DRAWING_TYPE and EXTRACTION_TARGET tuple.
DRAWING_EXTRACT is used for selective structured extraction from drawing pages rather than full-page transcription.
The DRAWING_EXTRACT architecture splits type-agnostic core phases from target-specific repertoire hooks.
Instruction files use the AGENT_* naming convention, while agent roles use role names such as DRAWING_EXTRACT.
DRAWING_EXTRACT has AGENT_TYPE TYPE 1.
DRAWING_EXTRACT has AGENT_CLASS PERSONA.
DRAWING_EXTRACT uses chat as its interaction surface.
DRAWING_EXTRACT write scope is WORK_DIR plus a target-aware SOURCE_DIR subtree.
DRAWING_EXTRACT may block while operating.
DRAWING_EXTRACT primary outputs include target-aware combined Markdown and CSV outputs, duplicate or reconciliation CSVs, validation or merge outputs, stubs, and a work manifest.
DRAWING_EXTRACT dispatches drawing-extract-page, drawing-titleblock-page, and pandid-valve-symbol-instance via the TASK shell.
PFD, DRAWING_SET, and P_AND_ID drawing types have implemented extraction targets.
Drawing types outside implemented PFD, DRAWING_SET, and P_AND_ID are registered as fail-fast stubs.
DRAWING_SET supports the implemented titleblock_index extraction target.
PFD supports the implemented top_equipment_header_basic extraction target.
PFD supports the implemented top_equipment_header_detailed extraction target.
P_AND_ID supports the implemented valve_count_basic extraction target.
P_AND_ID supports the implemented valve_count_detailed extraction target.
ISOMETRIC is registered as a fail-fast stub drawing type.
GA is registered as a fail-fast stub drawing type.

The valid DRAWING_EXTRACT target combinations are DRAWING_SET/titleblock_index, PFD/top_equipment_header_basic, PFD/top_equipment_header_detailed, P_AND_ID/valve_count_basic, and P_AND_ID/valve_count_detailed.
Any DRAWING_TYPE and EXTRACTION_TARGET combination outside the valid set rejects during Phase 0 pre-flight.
When DRAWING_TYPE is ISOMETRIC or GA, the orchestrator rejects the run as registered but not implemented.
Stubbed drawing types create no work directory, perform no rasterization, and generate no crops.
Operators specify only DRAWING_TYPE and EXTRACTION_TARGET; the orchestrator resolves the skill and deterministic tool chain.
DRAWING_SET/titleblock_index uses prepare_titleblock_crops.py, drawing-titleblock-page, build_titleblock_page_brief.py, titleblock validators, and titleblock assembly outputs.
PFD/top_equipment_header_basic uses prepare_header_crops.py, drawing-extract-page, build_page_worker_brief.py, PFD validators, equipment assembly, Markdown assembly, and duplicate flags.
PFD/top_equipment_header_detailed uses prepare_header_crops.py, drawing-extract-page, detailed schema validation, PFD assembly and QC, and optional merge tools.

P_AND_ID/valve_count_basic uses prepare_pandid_tiles.py, pandid-valve-symbol-instance, valve tile validators, candidate assembly, geometry duplicate assignment, count aggregation, duplicate flags, and _LATEST.md.
P_AND_ID/valve_count_detailed uses the valve tile pipeline plus basic-vs-detailed reconciliation.
PDF_PATH is a required absolute path to the input PDF.
SOURCE_DIR defaults to the parent of PDF_PATH and receives the target-aware per-page and assembled outputs.
WORK_DIR defaults to a sibling drawing_extract_work directory for rasterized page images and helper crops.
START_PAGE and END_PAGE are required inclusive bounds for the page scope.
DPI defaults to 400 for rasterization.
BATCH_SIZE defaults to 5 TASK skill dispatches in parallel.
DRAWING_TYPE is a required drawing-type selector.
EXTRACTION_TARGET is a required target selector within the drawing type.
TILE_GRID defaults to 5x4 for P_AND_ID valve tiling, and 5x4 is the minimum production baseline unless the human accepts lower resolution.
OVERLAP_PX defaults to 200 pixels for read-box expansion around each emit box.
BODY_EXCLUSIONS defaults to border,titleblock; notes-column exclusion is opt-in because notes and insets may contain valve symbols.
MINI_GRID defaults to 5x5 and workers emit locations as A1 through E5 rather than pixel coordinates.
ALLOW_REFERENCE_SHEETS defaults to false, causing legend or reference sheets that reach dispatch to return NO_FINDINGS_REFERENCE.
SCOPE_FILE should be supplied for P_AND_ID production runs and normally comes from an edited scope_proposal.md.
BASIC_REFERENCE_RUN may identify the explicit basic run folder used as the comparison reference for detailed runs.
BASIC_COUNTS_CSV is required when producing a basic-vs-detailed reconciliation report.
top_equipment_header_detailed requires REQUESTED_KNOWN_FIELDS, EXTRA_FIELDS, and REQUIRED_FIELDS runtime parameters.
The v2 known-field catalog contains equipment_type, equipment_description, capacity_text, and power_text.
MERGE_EXISTING_DATA defaults to false and enables merging the combined CSV against EXISTING_DATA_PATH when true.
EXISTING_DATA_PATH is required only when MERGE_EXISTING_DATA is true.
MERGE_KEY defaults to equipment_number and only equipment_number is supported in v2.
EXTRACTION_MODE is a deprecated runtime alias, and only top_equipment_header_with_dwg is accepted.
The legacy alias top_equipment_header_with_dwg remaps to DRAWING_TYPE=PFD and EXTRACTION_TARGET=top_equipment_header_basic.
OUTPUT_FORMAT was removed from the v2 runtime surface.
Per-page output is always markdown_stub in v2.
Combined outputs are always produced in both CSV and Markdown in v2.
When EXTRACTION_MODE=top_equipment_header_with_dwg is provided, DRAWING_EXTRACT emits a deprecation warning.
The compatibility shim sets DRAWING_TYPE=PFD and EXTRACTION_TARGET=top_equipment_header_basic before normal Phase 0 validation.
Unknown legacy EXTRACTION_MODE values reject with a message directing operators to DRAWING_TYPE and EXTRACTION_TARGET.
When both legacy and new parameters are provided, the new DRAWING_TYPE and EXTRACTION_TARGET parameters take precedence.
Rasterization in DRAWING_EXTRACT is deterministic and resumable.
Page and tile image interpretation is delegated to target-specific TASK skills rather than performed directly by DRAWING_EXTRACT.
DRAWING_TYPE and EXTRACTION_TARGET are validated before rasterization or crop work begins.
Per-page artifacts are written under {SOURCE_DIR}/{DRAWING_TYPE}/{EXTRACTION_TARGET}/.
P_AND_ID and drawing-set run-scoped artifacts are written under immutable RUN folders.
_LATEST.md is a convenience pointer rather than an authority marker.
Existing per-page stubs are reusable only when their YAML frontmatter matches the current run tuple.
File existence alone is insufficient for resume safety.
NO_FINDINGS is a valid page outcome and must be preserved in reporting.
NO_FINDINGS_REFERENCE is a valid P_AND_ID valve outcome for legend or reference sheets that reach dispatch.
Failed pages must be reported explicitly and must not be silently omitted.
Combined outputs must be assembled only from per-page stubs generated for the current extraction scope.
Combined outputs must preserve drawing, system_name, and source_page provenance fields.
Combined outputs and duplicate reporting must be produced by deterministic tools.
Crop preparation, stub-count reporting, and sanitization must run for every PFD run before assembly.
NO_FINDINGS and very low-count pages must be treated skeptically until helper crops and stub-count reports support the result.
Per-page CSV output is not supported.
DRAWING_EXTRACT precedence orders protocol before spec, spec before structure, and structure before rationale.
DRAWING_EXTRACT core phases apply to every drawing type.
DRAWING_EXTRACT hook phases dispatch target-specific tools according to the target dispatch table and hook registry.
Phase 0 applies the compatibility shim when EXTRACTION_MODE is provided.
Phase 0 rejects unknown drawing types with a message listing implemented and stubbed valid drawing types.
Phase 0 rejects ISOMETRIC and GA before creating a work directory or generating rasterization or crops.
Phase 0 rejects an EXTRACTION_TARGET that is invalid for the selected DRAWING_TYPE.
For top_equipment_header_detailed, Phase 0 validates REQUESTED_KNOWN_FIELDS against the v2 catalog.
For top_equipment_header_detailed, Phase 0 rejects EXTRA_FIELDS that collide with base columns, catalog fields, or duplicate names.
For top_equipment_header_detailed, Phase 0 requires REQUIRED_FIELDS to be a subset of requested known fields and extra field names.
For P_AND_ID runs, a provided SCOPE_FILE pre-filters pages before dispatch.
For P_AND_ID runs without SCOPE_FILE, execution should proceed only for intentional exploratory or diagnostic page ranges.
For valve_count_detailed, BASIC_COUNTS_CSV is required only when reconciliation is requested.
Phase 0 validates that PDF_PATH exists, is readable, and has a .pdf extension.
Phase 0 validates START_PAGE and END_PAGE against the PDF page count and ordering.
Phase 0 resolves SOURCE_DIR and WORK_DIR defaults.
Phase 0 creates WORK_DIR and the target-aware output subtree when needed.
Phase 0 creates or resolves immutable run folders for DRAWING_SET and P_AND_ID targets.
Phase 0 validates EXISTING_DATA_PATH and MERGE_KEY when MERGE_EXISTING_DATA is true.
Phase 0 reports resolved runtime values before starting work.
Phase 1 rasterizes only the requested page range with tools/pdf2md/rasterize_pdf.py.
Phase 1 reads the WORK_DIR manifest after rasterization.
Phase 1 confirms that every requested page has a corresponding PNG file.
Phase 1 reports how many pages were rendered and how many were reused.
For PFD targets, Phase 1.5 generates helper crops with prepare_header_crops.py using the drawing-type crop-spec registry.
The default PFD header crop geometry uses header_height_ratio=0.18.
The PFD top_header crop isolates the top-header band and excludes the right-side notes area.
PFD top_header_slice crops provide overlapping multiblock review segments.
The PFD titleblock crop isolates the title block.
Phase 1.5 confirms helper crops exist for every page in scope.
If helper crops cannot be generated for a page, DRAWING_EXTRACT reports the page and continues with caution.
For DRAWING_SET/titleblock_index, Phase 1.5 generates four corner crops and a full-page thumbnail.
For P_AND_ID valve targets, Phase 1.5 generates tiles with prepare_pandid_tiles.py.
P_AND_ID tile preparation writes tile images, per-page tile manifests, a run-level tile_manifest.json, and runs validate_tile_partition.py as a self-check.
P_AND_ID emit boxes must exactly tile the body box with no overlap.
P_AND_ID read boxes must contain emit boxes.
The per-page crop override workflow allows page-scoped header-height-ratio overrides when extraction under-captures due to crop geometry.
Only crops for the specified override page are overwritten during a crop override.
After a page crop override, the operator deletes the affected stub and re-dispatches with the same run parameters so only that page re-extracts.
Per-page crop override decisions are logged in page_crop_overrides.md beside WORK_DIR.
Phase 2 builds the ordered page list from START_PAGE through END_PAGE.
For P_AND_ID valve targets, Phase 2 filters pages by accepted P_AND_ID scope unless the run is forced diagnostic.
For each PFD page, Phase 2 derives full-page image, header crop, titleblock crop, header slices, and target-aware output stub paths.
For drawing-set inventory, Phase 2 derives titleblock crop paths, thumbnail path, and the output path in the run folder.
For P_AND_ID valve targets, Phase 2 derives tile_id, tile image path, tile geometry, and output path from tile_manifest.json.
Phase 2 resume-safety validation is required before dispatch.
A reusable existing stub must match current drawing_type, extraction_target, source_pdf, and source_page frontmatter.
Detailed-target reusable stubs must also match requested_known_fields, requested_extra_fields, and required_fields.
Phase 2 invokes the target-appropriate deterministic resume validator before reusing existing stubs.
Resume validator exit code 0 means resume safety is OK and passing stubs may be reused.
Resume validator exit code 1 means one or more stubs mismatch the current run tuple and the orchestrator must reject the run.
Resume validator exit code 2 means setup error and the orchestrator must surface and halt.
Missing stubs are skipped by resume validation and queued for extraction.
DRAWING_SET inventory uses validate_titleblock_resume_metadata.py for resume validation.
P_AND_ID valve targets use validate_valve_tile_resume_metadata.py with tile_manifest.json for resume validation.
Changing tile grid, body box, read boxes, emit boxes, overlap, or mode makes previous P_AND_ID valve stubs non-reusable.
Phase 2 queues pages whose stubs are missing or selected for operator-requested re-extraction.
Worker dispatches must use the TASK shell with the TaskSkill resolved by the target dispatch table.
The TASK shell loads SKILL.md, BRIEF_SCHEMA.md, and companion files such as QA_CHECKS.md and TOOL_POLICY.md when present.
Each dispatch brief must follow the INIT-TASK shape documented in AGENT_TASK.md.
Each dispatch brief includes TaskSkill, RuntimeOverrides, AllowedWriteTargets, and ExpectedOutputs.
The orchestrator should include CustomInstructions from BRIEF_SCHEMA.md as defense-in-depth reminders.
build_page_worker_brief.py emits a valid INIT-TASK brief for PFD page workers.
Non-TASK dispatch surfaces should inline contract-critical content and canonical templates only as a fallback.
Phase 2 divides queued pages into batches of BATCH_SIZE.
Phase 2 spawns TASK dispatches in parallel for each batch and collects page or tile RUN_STATUS values.
Phase 2 classifies each page or tile as SUCCESS, NO_FINDINGS, NO_FINDINGS_REFERENCE, FAILED, or FAILED_INPUTS.
Phase 2 reports batch progress after each batch.
After each batch, Phase 2 invokes the target-appropriate deterministic stub format validator.
A SUCCESS stub must include finding_count in frontmatter and parse to exactly finding_count meaningful rows.
Missing finding_count or mismatch between finding_count and parsed rows is a format failure requiring re-dispatch.
Phase 2.5 uses extract_pdf_titleblock_text.py as an optional deterministic cross-check when the tool and pdftotext are available.
Title-block verification cross-checks DWG NO. and system_name candidates.
Unavailability of title-block verification tooling warns and continues without blocking page extraction.
Phase 2.6 runs report_stub_counts.py after page extraction and before sanitization.
The raw stub-count report is used as a deterministic skepticism gate.
For the basic target, QA flags pages with NO_FINDINGS, row_count <= 2, or blank_tag_count > 0.
For the detailed target, QA additionally reviews per-field populated counts, missing_required_fields, identical_value_flags, and round_trip_row_loss.
Any non-empty round_trip_row_loss is a blocking QA signal before sanitization.
QA-flagged pages must be scrutinized against helper crops before the run is treated as production-ready.
Phase 2.7 runs sanitize_equipment_stubs.py for PFD targets.
PFD stub sanitization may drop blank-tag rows.
PFD stub sanitization may drop obvious instrument, control, or note rows using deny-list filters.
PFD stub sanitization may trim equipment_name values to the primary equipment label.
PFD stub sanitization may convert pages to NO_FINDINGS when no valid tagged header rows remain.
For detailed targets, sanitization decisions apply only to base columns and pass detail columns through unchanged.
PFD stub sanitization must not invent new equipment rows.
The sanitizer refuses to overwrite a SUCCESS stub when finding_count is missing or parsed meaningful row count does not equal finding_count.
Every sanitizer overwrite is backed up in a run-scoped JSONL bundle.
When report-csv is provided, the sanitizer writes a per-page audit CSV.
Phase 2.7b runs validate_detailed_schema.py for top_equipment_header_detailed.
validate_detailed_schema.py exit code 1 indicates schema divergence across the page range.
Assembly must not proceed until detailed-target schema divergence is resolved.
For the basic target, Phase 2.7b is a no-op.
Phase 2.8 deterministic page-family recovery is opt-in only.
Recovery is valid only when replacement rows are derived from verified rendered page crops for a known repeated layout.
Recovery must overwrite only affected page stubs and preserve existing page-level provenance fields.
recover_deepcut_multiblock_headers.py is the Deepcut PFD recovery tool.
recover_deepcut_multiblock_headers.py currently reads legacy-format stubs and should only be invoked in legacy-domain recovery scenarios.
Phase 2.8b backfills weak title-block system_name extraction from an operator correction CSV.
System-name backfill overwrites system_name in targeted stub YAML frontmatter and row cells through parse/render round-trip.
System-name backfill must run before Phase 3 assembly.
System-name backfill is idempotent when re-run with the same mapping.
Phase 2.9 runs report_stub_counts.py after sanitization and optional recovery.
The final stub-count report identifies NO_FINDINGS pages and residual low-count, blank-tag, or detail-capture issues.
Phase 3 writes target-aware combined Markdown, combined CSV, and duplicate-flag CSV paths.
PFD equipment targets build the combined CSV with assemble_equipment_csv.py.
PFD equipment targets build the combined Markdown with assemble_equipment_markdown.py.
PFD equipment targets build duplicate flags with flag_duplicate_equipment_csv.py keyed by equipment_number.
Duplicate flags are QA candidates and do not automatically collapse or remove rows.
dedupe_equipment_csv.py may be used only for optional or manual downstream workflows, not default production output.
Basic PFD combined CSV columns are equipment_number, equipment_name, system_name, drawing, and source_page.
Detailed PFD combined CSV columns extend base columns with requested known fields, extra fields, and source_page.
DRAWING_SET/titleblock_index assembly writes inventory CSV, inventory Markdown, scope_proposal.md, and updates _LATEST.md.
The operator may edit or copy scope_proposal.md and pass it as SCOPE_FILE for P_AND_ID valve runs.
P_AND_ID valve targets assemble candidates, assign geometry duplicates, aggregate counts, and flag duplicate true tags.
P_AND_ID duplicate true tags are QA review candidates rather than automatic errors.
P_AND_ID line and spec text is excluded from duplicate-tag review and reported through tag-quality metrics.
Basic P_AND_ID output validation is optional before using a run as the detailed-pass reference.
For P_AND_ID valve_count_detailed, Phase 3.1 compares detailed counts to an explicit basic counts CSV when provided.
Basic-vs-detailed reconciliation defaults to RECONCILE_REVIEW when absolute delta is greater than 2 and absolute delta percent is greater than 10.
NO_FINDINGS_REFERENCE pages are excluded from basic-vs-detailed reconciliation.
When MERGE_EXISTING_DATA is true, Phase 3.5 merges the new combined CSV against EXISTING_DATA_PATH.
Phase 3.5 flags post-merge conflicts using flag_merge_conflicts.py.
PFD equipment merge is repertoire-scoped and supports only equipment_number as the merge key in v2.
PFD equipment merge performs no automatic conflict resolution.
PFD equipment merge outputs merge_result, merge_conflicts, merge_unmatched_extracted, and merge_unmatched_existing CSVs.
Phase 4 reports drawing_type, extraction_target, target-aware output paths, pages processed, NO_FINDINGS pages, failed pages, extracted rows, and duplicate flags.
For detailed targets, Phase 4 reports per-field capture counts and required-field warnings.
For merged runs, Phase 4 reports merge conflict and unmatched counts.
Phase 4 identifies failed pages explicitly.
Phase 4 reiterates the compatibility shim deprecation warning when EXTRACTION_MODE was remapped.
The implemented hook registry consolidates the tool invoked at each hook point for each implemented target.

PFD basic and detailed targets use the same crop prep, page-worker skill, title-block verification, sanitization, recovery fallback, assembly, metadata backfill, duplicate flagging, optional dedupe, and merge hooks.
The PFD detailed target adds detailed stub-count metrics and validate_detailed_schema.py schema-consistency validation.
DRAWING_SET/titleblock_index uses titleblock crop prep, drawing-titleblock-page, titleblock brief building, titleblock validation, titleblock assembly, and scope_proposal.md for operator review.

P_AND_ID valve targets use P_AND_ID tile prep, pandid-valve-symbol-instance, valve tile briefs, valve tile validation, candidate assembly, aggregation, geometry duplicate assignment, and duplicate tag flags.
P_AND_ID valve_count_detailed should preferably use tiling matched to the basic run used for comparison.
P_AND_ID valve_count_detailed includes optional review of RECONCILIATION_REPORT.md.
A new drawing type must add registry entries in AGENT_DRAWING_EXTRACT.md and the drawing-extract-page skill contract.
A new drawing type must register crop geometry in prepare_header_crops.py or add new crop kinds as needed.
A new drawing type must extend the drawing-extract-page skill target semantics for extraction region, fields, and rules.
A new drawing type must add or refactor assembly tools for its target columns.
A new drawing type must provide target-appropriate QA and sanitization hooks.
A new drawing type must choose a natural duplicate or merge key and add a dedicated merge tool if supported.
A new drawing type should run a crop-adequacy spike on representative drawings before production use.
A new drawing type requires W1 schema core tests and tool-specific regression fixtures where warranted.
Adding a drawing type should extend hook mappings without changing the core protocol.
The core protocol remains stable when new drawing types are added; only target hook branches gain new mappings.
DRAWING_EXTRACT validity is specified by S1 through S12.
S1 requires stubbed drawing types to reject at pre-flight with no rasterization, crops, or work-dir side effects.
S2 requires every page or tile in scope to be classified as SUCCESS, NO_FINDINGS, NO_FINDINGS_REFERENCE, FAILED, or FAILED_INPUTS.
S3 requires page or tile image interpretation to be performed by target-specific TASK skill dispatches.
S4 requires stubs to be written at target-aware paths or immutable run-folder paths, not legacy top-level paths.
S5 requires existing stubs to be reused only when frontmatter matches the full current parameter tuple.
S6 requires target combined outputs to exist at target-aware paths unless every page or tile failed.
S7 requires NO_FINDINGS pages to be recorded explicitly and reported to the human.
S8 requires combined outputs to preserve drawing, system_name, and source_page fields.
S9 requires validate_detailed_schema.py to exit 0 before top_equipment_header_detailed assembly runs.
S10 requires helper crops, slice generation, stub-count reporting, and deterministic sanitization for PFD targets unless the run fails earlier.
S11 requires a deprecation warning when EXTRACTION_MODE=top_equipment_header_with_dwg is provided.
S12 requires merged runs to include result, conflicts, unmatched-extracted, and unmatched-existing outputs.
The spec-satisfaction matrix distinguishes hard evidence from process evidence.
Hard evidence is a deterministic tool exit code or file existence proof.
Process evidence shows that a phase ran and produced output consistent with a condition without independently proving it.
The STRUCTURE section defines WORK_DIR and SOURCE_DIR filesystem layouts.
WORK_DIR contains rasterization manifests, page images, helper crops, QA reports, sanitizer reports, recovery reports, and tile or titleblock crop manifests.
SOURCE_DIR contains target-aware DRAWING_TYPE and EXTRACTION_TARGET subtrees with stubs, combined outputs, duplicate flags, run folders, and optional merge outputs.
The tool dependency table maps deterministic tools to the DRAWING_EXTRACT phase that uses them.

Rasterize, crop-prep, resume validation, stub parsing, brief building, QA, sanitization, schema validation, assembly, duplicate flagging, reconciliation, and merge tools are declared deterministic dependencies.
The dispatched skills are drawing-extract-page, drawing-titleblock-page, and pandid-valve-symbol-instance.
drawing-extract-page performs PFD equipment page extraction.
drawing-titleblock-page performs single-page titleblock inventory extraction.
pandid-valve-symbol-instance performs P_AND_ID pixel-anchored valve symbol-instance extraction.
DRAWING_EXTRACT separates drawing-aware structured extraction from PDF-to-Markdown transcription.
DRAWING_EXTRACT targets tables and CSVs rather than narrative Markdown.
DRAWING_EXTRACT treats title blocks and header regions as more important than reading order.
NO_FINDINGS is a normal expected page outcome in the DRAWING_EXTRACT success model.
DRAWING_EXTRACT is intended for repeatable field extraction across drawing sets with the same target tuple.
DRAWING_EXTRACT favors crop-first multiblock review plus deterministic QC because undercounted pages create downstream work.
Engineering drawing families have different semantics, header layouts, identity keys, and extraction targets.
The core-vs-repertoire split isolates rasterization, path resolution, resume safety, schema consistency, and reporting from target-specific crop, QA, sanitization, assembly, and merge behavior.
New drawing types can plug hooks into the core protocol without rewriting the orchestrator.
Per-page CSV output was retired because the assembler expects csv.DictReader headers on line 1 and no parser contract exists for CSV preamble metadata.
Self-describing markdown_stub files carry schema metadata needed by resume-safety validation and deterministic assembly.
Target-aware subdirectories prevent basic and detailed runs against the same PDF from overwriting each other.
Resume-safety validates stub frontmatter rather than file existence to prevent false reuse under parameter drift.
Stubbed drawing types fail fast to prevent users from believing unsupported drawing types are producing valid extraction.
The fail-fast path for stubbed drawing types costs about 100 ms and surfaces the extension-point walkthrough.
Merging PFD equipment datasets on equipment_number is a PFD-equipment repertoire operation.
Other repertoires can have different identity keys and conflict semantics than PFD equipment.
A generic merge-with-configurable-keys abstraction would over-claim generality in v2.
PDF2MD remains focused on transcription while DRAWING_EXTRACT provides a dedicated drawing workflow contract.
The PFD equipment header region is a spatially arranged collection of tag and name clusters rather than a table.
Extracting PFD equipment headers requires distinguishing equipment tags, instrument tags, notes, and setpoints.
Extracting PFD equipment headers requires associating descriptor lines with parent equipment blocks.
Extracting PFD equipment headers requires deciding where one equipment block ends and another begins.
Extracting PFD equipment headers requires classifying values such as 3 x 33 percent by semantic role.
The core difficulty of PFD equipment header extraction is semantic association rather than glyph recognition.
The VLM performs visual-spatial interpretation while deterministic tools operate on the resulting structured output.
Title-block text extraction uses pdftotext only as an optional cross-check because title blocks are more regular and text-centric than equipment headers.
The VLM page worker remains authoritative for DWG NO. and system_name.
Sanitization uses closed-vocabulary checks that do not require visual reasoning.
Assembly, validation, duplicate flagging, and merge are rule-based data operations on structured rows.
DRAWING_EXTRACT uses VLMs for visual-spatial drawing interpretation and deterministic tools for rule-expressible structured data operations.
Header crops preserve effective resolution by concentrating the input on the extraction region.
Header crops improve legibility of small detail lines such as capacity, power, and equipment description.
Crops enforce extraction region discipline by physically removing process body and notes regions.
Overlapping header slices mitigate the failure mode where a VLM stops before extracting the right side of a wide header.
Items at far-right or lower-row header positions can be prominent in slices but missed in the full header image.
The full-page image is permitted as secondary context for resolving spatial ambiguity, but detail discovery must come from crops.
The header_height_ratio parameter is tunable because crops can miss items below the crop line.
Dense pages may require a header_height_ratio of 0.22 or higher.
